origin_and_geography.native_tract: Pulikulam, Sivagangai, Madurai, Dindigul, and Virudhunagar districts of Southern Tamil Nadu, India.
origin_and_geography.agro_climatic_zone: Southern semi-arid red soil dry plains.
origin_and_geography.historical_background: Also known as Jallikattu Madu or Palingu Madu. Bred traditionally by pastoral communities for agile field work, penning in agricultural fields for bio-manure (Kidaari penning), and the traditional bull-embracing sport of Jallikattu.

morphological_traits.horns: Curved backward and outward, sharply pointed and forward-directed at the tip, highly defensive.
morphological_traits.forehead: Narrow with a distinct depression in the center.
morphological_traits.coat_color: Greyish white or light grey in cows; bulls are dark grey or black with white patches on face and extremities.
morphological_traits.ears: Short, erect, horizontal, highly responsive to sounds.
morphological_traits.hump_and_dewlap: Small to medium firm muscular hump; tight, well-tucked dewlap.
morphological_traits.body_conformation: Small, compact, lean frame; long muscular legs, exceptionally quick reflexes and speed.

production_and_utility.primary_utility: High-agility draught, migratory field penning for organic manure, and Jallikattu sporting events.
production_and_utility.draught_capacity: Remarkable sprint speed, quick turning ability, and endurance under blazing tropical sun.

management_and_resilience.diet_and_forage: Naturally scavenges on dry scrublands, weeds, and post-harvest crop stubble; minimal supplementary concentrate needed.
management_and_resilience.disease_resistance: Extraordinary resistance to tropical diseases and ticks; withstands prolonged dehydration and heat.
management_and_resilience.temperament: Fiery, aggressive when threatened, alert, highly territorial.

conservation_status: Registered as an indigenous breed by ICAR-NBAGR in 2012; protected under Tamil Nadu animal welfare and heritage initiatives.
